title: Dedicated: Fix tenant isolation and intermittent VPC/DNS routing failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers running Redwood Dedicated reported intermittent cross-tenant connectivity and DNS resolution failures after a recent VPC peering optimization rollout. Symptoms included: (1) tenant A occasionally receiving 502/504s when traffic routed through peered subnets, (2) internal service discovery failing for retried requests (DNS NXDOMAIN or stale A records), and (3) one customer observing cross-tenant metrics leaking into their network egress accounting. This ticket tracks investigation, hotfixes, and a safe rollout for the Dedicated fleet.
steps_taken: 2026-02-15: On-call triaged initial support ticket SUP-7192 — identified error spike in dedicated-east-1 cluster serving rented GPU pools.
2026-02-16: Reproduced customer 502s in staging with a traffic replay; observed ephemeral TCP resets between worker instances in peered subnets.
2026-02-18: Rolled back a platform-level VPC route optimization change (optimize-peers-v1) on the affected region — error rate dropped ~60% for one customer.
2026-02-20: Collected packet captures and DNS query logs; found TTL mismatches and a race in the internal DNS cache invalidation logic when peer mappings changed during autoscaling events.
2026-02-25: Built and tested a unit patch to the Dedicated network controller to add serializable updates for peer route table writes and a stronger lease for DNS cache entries.
2026-03-03: Deployed canary of network-controller-v1.2.4 to two low-traffic Dedicated pools — monitoring showed no regression and stable DNS TTL behavior.
2026-03-08: Customer-facing canary with a single paying Dedicated tenant in us-west-2; verified no request errors for 72h under peak load.
2026-03-10: Preparing a staged rollout plan and additional validation tests before full region rollout.
root_cause: A concurrency bug in the Dedicated network controller allowed overlapping writes to peering route tables during autoscaling and maintenance windows. This caused transient route flaps and inconsistent neighbor announcements combined with a too-short DNS cache lease on the node-level resolver, amplifying transient NXDOMAIN responses and stale name resolution under retry storms.
rollback_plan: If post-rollout regression observed, immediately revert network-controller to v1.2.2 (previous stable) via Infrastructure orchestration (terraform apply -var-file=regions.json revert-network-controller) and re-enable the previous route write lock. Notify affected customers and open a high-priority support bridge.
deployment_plan: Stage 0: final runbook validation and playbook sign-off by SRE and Security (ETA 2026-03-11)
Stage 1: Canary in 2 low-traffic Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 (6 hours smoke + 48 hours monitoring)
Stage 2: Canary with 1 paid Dedicated customer per region (us-west-2, eu-central-1) for 72 hours
Stage 3: Gradual 30% -> 60% -> 100% device rollouts per region with 2-hour wait windows and SLO/alert gating
Stage 4: Post-rollout 7-day elevated monitoring for DNS/NAT/peering metrics and billing integrity checks
qa_checks: Integration test: repeated peer create/delete while running traffic replay with at least 100 concurrent streams — assert no route flaps.
E2E test: DNS resolution stability test for autoscaling events (assert >99.99% success within 50ms).
Load test: simulate customer retry storm to ensure no cross-tenant metric leakage and correct per-tenant egress tagging.
Security test: validate RBAC on peering operations and that no tenant ID is exposed in route table tags.
